recipes.name: Awesome Honey Pecan Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 1.25 pounds boneless pork loin, pounded thin

steps.text: In a shallow dish, mix together flour, salt and pepper. Dredge pork cutlets in the flour mixture.
In a large skillet, melt butter over medium-high heat. Add chops, and brown both sides. Transfer to a warm plate.
Mix honey and pecans into the pan drippings. Heat through, stirring constantly. Pour sauce over cutlets.

raw_recipe.headline: Awesome Honey Pecan Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: A glaze of warm honey and pecans makes thin and tender pork loin cutlets extra yummy. Be careful not to overcook the pork or the sauce. A light touch is the key.

video.description: Take your weekly pork chop dinner to the next flavor level with this simple recipe that’s perfect for making on busy weeknights. Simply dredge pork cutlets in flour seasoned with salt and pepper, then brown them in hot butter. Finally, stir honey and chopped pecans into the pan drippings and pour it on the chops and serve with potatoes and green veggies.

review.reviewBody: Delicious! Husband loved them! I took others' advice and doubled the butter and added 1/4 cup maple syrup. I used finely chopped pecans which worked well. (Do not double the pecans, 1/4 cup was ample.) I had lots of flour left over, so next time will reduce flour to 1/3 cup.

We had this over the weekend. Following the advice of other reviewers: I added about 1/2 cups sliced onion and 1/2 tsp minced garlic in while browning the pork chops. I also added a 1/4 cup of chicken broth and 1 tsp soy sauce (this, then made it more of a sauce than a glaze). I did not toast the pecans. These pork chops and sauce were amazing! I served it with mashed potatoes and green beans. There were no leftovers!

Just as another cook did, I added 1/4 cup pure maple syrup for sauce PLUS I added 1/4 cup sliced green onion tops and browned in the butter prior to adding the syrup and honey. Do not over cook your pork so it remain moist. Be sure to simmer the sauce until it thickens. Finely chopped pecans work best.

Delicious! Just made a few changes: added 1/2 tsp sage, 1/2 tsp cajun spice, and 1/2 tsp ground ginger, along with salt and pepper, to the flour mixture; added a few dashes ginger and cajun spice to the pecan mixture using maple syrup instead of honey. Also, we seared the chops and then baked them for 25-30 minutes at 350° until cooked thouroughly. Then poured the pecans/syrup mixture over. SO GOOD.

This was an excellent recipe. I did take the advice from others and made the following changes. I made it with 4 med. boneless pork chops. I added salt and pepper to the flour mixture. I sautéed 1/4 cup chopped onions and 4 cloves garlic before adding the honey and pecans. I also added some white wine and a couple of drops of chili sauce to the sauce. It was so good. I will add this to our meal rotation. Thank you for a fantastic recipe.

This recipe was quick and very easy. I did add soy sauce, maple syrup along with the honey and pecans. I stirred it till the sauce caramelized a bit, then I put the pork chops back in for a bit. I really liked the combo of salty and sweet I ended up with. Will be making this again.

Boyo's and Girlo's and folks what a great dinner, made as per recipe just added two more pork fillets with a extra tablespoon of butter. Fantastic served with mashed sweet potato and green beans both drizzled with the sauce.
Note: pounded the pork fillets to about 10mm or 3/8 inches
thick pan fried 3-4 minutes one side and 2 minutes the other side then let sit while mashing and microwaving the
cut beans
The only change I made was I broiled the pork chops after topping them with the mixture and it caramelized the honey and pecans onto the chops so good
I just pan fried our chops with salt, pepper, and garlic, adding the honey and pecans at the end. Huge hit in my house, we loved it!

Very easy and tasty. Used thin cut boneless porkchops. Cooked very quickly and remained tender. Used a large nonstick frypan and returned the browned chops to the pecan honey mixture to keep it warm. Served with roasted red potatoes and fresh peas. Will make again as it is so easy.

My family loved this recipe. I cut a pork tenderloin up and pounded the slices a little thin. I did add a splash of soy sauce and white wine. After I made the sauce I put my meet back in the pan with lid and let it simmer on low for 5 minutes... YUM!! The meat was so tender and not super sweet. A great new way to use Tenderloin instead of just roasting the whole thing. THanks!!!!
My husband, chef Pierre, helped cook this lovely meal. Followed recipe and was delicious @
My pork chops were over an inch thick, so I cut them in half. They got up to 140 degrees pretty quickly without drying out. My wife was impressed. Can't beat that!!!

Double the sauce!! This is definitely a keeper! So delicious as is. I added cayenne pepper for the irresistible sweet hot combo as another reviewer suggested. Next time I’ll add even more cayenne and double the sauce so that there’s enough to drizzle over the rice I made as a side dish. So good!!
My husband loves this recipe. I add a little cayenne to my flour for a little punch.
Easy dinner. Delicious!

I made this without the flour coating 
and seasoned the porkchops woth onion and garlic powder as well. also accidentally made too much of the sauce because I forgot I wasn't using as much meat pretty god, very simple not my favorite flavors personally but im a real picky eater
I loved the ease of preparation & enjoyed the dish. It was a nice change however hubby didn’t care for it at all so I probably won’t be making this one again.
Excellent weekday dinner! I serve with baked sweet potatoes and a vegetable. Quick and easy and delish!
Cook time was vague but assumed 5 minutes per side. These were a little overdone. 4 minutes a side probably would have been perfect. Taste was very good.
